title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: scope just-in-time audit to users and groups
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's planned audit-scoping change, including continued logging for block-scope users and the December rollout recommendations. The first control's path stops on the correct settings page; extending it to the audit setting described in the notice would make it easier to follow.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans user and group inclusion or exclusion for Endpoint DLP JIT Audit.
claims.quote: Enable customers to include or exclude users/user groups from Just‑In‑Time (JIT) Audit, ensuring audits are generated only for the selected users or groups.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: Previously, enabling JIT automatically logged activity for users not targeted by policies.
claims.quote: Previously, when Just-in-time protection was turned on, user activities were logged automatically for users who were not targeted by policies.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The notice says audit logging must be explicitly configured using the selected audit scope.
claims.quote: With this update, audit logging must be explicitly configured so that only users or groups included in the audit scope have their activities logged.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview portal route Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection reaches the page holding the audit and block scoping controls.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal.
2. Select Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection.
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path and the corresponding rendered table path to 'Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection > Devices > Audit covered user activities'. Retain the note attributing the Devices tab and audit setting to MC1387575, which supplies those final steps.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The notice places Audit covered user activities on the Devices tab of the Just-in-time protection settings page and instructs admins to turn it on.
claims.quote: Just-in-time audit behavior is now managed through the Audit covered user activities setting under Settings > Data loss prevention > Just-in-time protection. Under the Devices tab, turn on Audit covered user activities.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Users included in audit scope see no JIT enforcement actions.
claims.quote: Users included in audit scope will not see enforcement actions

claims.claim: Audit-scope users have their activities recorded in Activity explorer.
claims.quote: Users included in audit scope will not see enforcement actions, and their activities will be recorded in Activity explorer.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Block-scope users are prevented from completing actions while files are evaluated for sensitive information.
claims.quote: Users included in block scope will be prevented from completing actions while files are evaluated for sensitive information.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Block-scope users also have their activities recorded in Activity explorer.
claims.quote: Users included in block scope will be prevented from completing actions while files are evaluated for sensitive information. Their activities are recorded in Activity explorer.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Users outside both audit and block scope have no JIT-covered activities recorded.
claims.quote: Users not included in audit or block scope will not have activities covered by Just-in-time protection recorded.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: No separate licence specific to JIT audit scoping is published in the checked Microsoft material.
claims.quote: Searched: "Endpoint DLP" "JIT" "licensing" "audit"; opened the Purview service description, endpoint-dlp-getting-started, endpoint-dlp-get-started-jit and endpoint-dlp-learn-about-jit; read MC1387575. No scoping-specific licence found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No meter or price specific to JIT audit scoping is documented in the checked Microsoft material.
claims.quote: Searched: "Purview" "just-in-time" "audit" "price" licensing; opened the Purview service description and both JIT Learn pages; read MC1387575. No JIT audit-scoping meter or price found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The audit-scoping control's arrival state and migration behavior without administrator action are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "Endpoint DLP" "JIT audit" "default" "scope"; "just-in-time protection" "default" "audit". Opened both JIT Learn pages; read the roadmap and MC1387575. Explicit configuration is required, but no initial switch value or scope migration is stated.

claims.claim: The JIT Learn pages do not yet describe Audit covered user activities or its exact inclusion and exclusion options.
claims.quote: Searched: "Audit covered user activities"; opened https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/endpoint-dlp-get-started-jit and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/endpoint-dlp-learn-about-jit. Neither describes that setting or its inclusion/exclusion options.

claims.where: Scope: Roles; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn's JIT pages name no role required to change this setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "just-in-time protection" "role"; opened https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/endpoint-dlp-get-started-jit and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/endpoint-dlp-learn-about-jit. Neither names a role for editing the setting.

claims.claim: No PowerShell, Graph or other API operation for configuring JIT audit and block scope was found.
claims.quote: Searched: "just-in-time protection" "PowerShell"; "Purview" "just-in-time protection" "Graph" API settings; "Audit covered user activities". Opened both JIT Learn pages and read returned API excerpts; none documents a JIT scope-setting operation.

claims.claim: No PowerShell, Graph or other API operation for changing the JIT Devices monitoring location was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview "just-in-time protection" "PowerShell" "Graph" settings Devices audit scope role; "Purview" "just-in-time protection" "Graph" API settings. Opened both JIT Learn pages; no operation setting the Devices monitoring location was found.

claims.claim: In the Microsoft Purview portal, Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection > Choose which locations to monitor > Devices selects the monitored location, not the audit-user scope.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal.
2. Select Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection.
3. Under Choose which locations to monitor, select the checkbox next to Devices.

claims.claim: Learn supplies an Advanced hunting query that reports antimalware client versions.
claims.quote: To find out which devices have the necessary antimalware client, go to Security portal > Investigation & response > Advanced hunting, and run this query.

claims.claim: Learn describes checking a device's JIT prerequisite through the Diagnostics page.
claims.quote: You can also go to Data Loss Prevention > Diagnostics page, and select Endpoint DLP not working card to check whether a specific device meets JIT prerequisite.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing the existing JIT configuration to identify users generating audit events.
claims.quote: Review your existing Just-in-time configuration to identify users currently generating audit events.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends explicitly adding all users or groups that should continue generating JIT audit events to audit scope.
claims.quote: Explicitly add all users or groups that should continue generating Just-in-time audit events to the audit scope.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends validating that expected activities appear in Activity explorer.
claims.quote: Validate your configuration to ensure expected activities appear in Activity explorer.
